passage:
The following text is adapted from Charlotte Brontë's 1847 novel Jane Eyre.

I had not intended to love him; the reader knows I had wrought hard to extirpate from my soul the germs of love there detected; and now, at the first renewed view of him, they spontaneously revived, green and strong!
stem: As used in the text, what does the word “extirpate” most nearly mean?
steps: She had “wrought hard” against love she didn't intend, and now the “germs” revive.
Reviving implies they had been fought against, as if uprooted.
So “extirpate” means to remove or root out completely.
key: Use the contrast: something she worked against now “revived.”
